libraryPreparationPreflight.agent_guidance: Exercise ConfidentialClientApplication/PublicClientApplication builder paths, token cache (de)serialization, and claims/authority parsing without contacting a live Azure AD tenant. If HTTP interaction needs to be exercised reflectively, stub it with an in-process com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer or mock the HTTP client rather than reaching out to login.microsoftonline.com; do not use real tenant credentials or introduce a live-network integration test.
risks: msal4j exposes integrated Windows auth and broker support that rely on native/OS-specific code paths (JNA, WAM broker); these are unlikely to be reachable or meaningfully testable in this Linux CI/native-image environment and may need to be left uncovered rather than forced.
libraryPreparationPreflight.summary: msal4j is a token-acquisition SDK (client-credentials, auth-code, device-code, ROPC flows) used entirely in-process. Its own upstream test suite (v1.15.0 pom) tests via Mockito-mocked HTTP interactions and builder/config assertions, not live Azure AD calls or containers. The already-shipped com.azure:azure-identity tests, which wrap msal4j for the same token-acquisition purpose, follow the identical pattern in this repo — self-contained builder/credential-chaining tests with no Docker image or extra Maven dependency, only the default assertj/junit scaffold.
